provider-neutral aggregation of owning-skill role_execution records with direct/delegated evidence, attempts, fallback, and final integration decisions

constraints: Do not claim standalone fallback output has the same quality as a matching downstream specialist skill or project-specific standard.

Do not replace downstream development skills; delegate requirement, specification, problem framing, architecture, test design, implementation, review, and compliance work to the matching local skill when the profile provides one.

Select the proportionate execution tier before requesting role evidence; require full role_execution records only for the full contract or explicit acceptance requirement, and aggregate actual returned evidence without taking domain ownership or inventing child invocation evidence.

Select the shared risk tier before delegated, external, or independent review execution. Require the validated packet and snapshot lease only when the full tier selects them; ordinary same-runtime work retains its bounded envelope. Bind external dispatch to its packet, preserve the one-tracked-writer boundary, integration owner and stop/retry limits, and never infer review criteria from dispatch prose.

Default to direct inline role execution. Select delegated only when every shared safety gate passes, at least one material-value trigger exists, cost/failure/retry risk supports delegation, and genuine invocation evidence is available.

If delegation is unsupported or fails, select direct when the shared inline-parity contract can be satisfied; otherwise record unavailable. Preserve attempt continuity and require new owner or workflow authorization for attempt three or later.
Compose a role_execution input envelope with an existing loaded_rule_ids packet only by reference; do not redefine its resolver, provider, effective-state, or rule semantics.
When no matching downstream skill exists, use fallback playbooks only to create a minimum viable checklist, handoff prompt, or quality gate.
When downstream skill mapping is inferred, report confidence and evidence before relying on the route.
Do not make a runtime goal or runtime workflow the source of truth for repository process rules; use runtime features to carry software-development-orchestrator execution.

Do not use this skill to orchestrate AI context audits, AI context governance, documentation-only cleanup, repository initialization, or other non-development maintenance workflows; route those tasks to their owning skill.

When workflow mode applies, follow .dev/standards/WORKFLOW-ARTIFACT-POLICY.md, default artifacts to .dev/workflows/<workflow-id>/, and keep the required locator there when a development workflow declares another repository-relative artifact root.
Do not store runtime workflow artifacts under .ai/assets/skills, .agents/skills, .claude/skills, generated folders, or temporary locations.
Preserve user decisions, explicit constraints, branch rules, commit policy, and validation expectations.
Create or switch to a dedicated workflow branch before creating development workflow artifacts or making material workflow edits; never use main as the active workflow branch.

Treat a requested pre-completion push or integration as a checkpoint and keep pending workflow state active without treating in_progress as an integration blocker; select linear or merge-commit topology under the target branch policy instead of deriving it from workflow mode.

Before creating separate workflows for multiple approved work items, evaluate delivery cohesion across outcome, branch, validation, reviewer and approval boundary, release horizon, and atomic rollback; one cohesive delivery may bind multiple work-item identifiers.
Treat one task or fewer than three substantive tasks as a workflow-value review signal, never as a reason to invent validation or closeout tasks.
Activate from high-level software-development intent; do not require the user to name this skill or downstream skills, and do not derive lifecycle stages from skill names alone.

When a requirement, design, or specification discussion awaits approval, pause before creating or executing implementation work; record the pending decision and resume only after explicit authorization.

Treat test-execution as an optional, unmapped capability contract. Resolve target-profile commands first, then a separately evaluated external skill, then the fallback contract; do not create or assume a dedicated test skill.
For test execution, use target-owned commands, working directory, prerequisites, and policy. Do not invent credentials, bypass controls, or escalate privileges implicitly.

Select unit and integration tests by default. Select E2E, browser, Playwright, and other environment-dependent tests only when target policy, requirements, an approved plan, or the owner requires them.

Record each selected test level as passed, failed, blocked-by-environment, not-applicable, or deferred-with-owner. Blocked-by-environment is never passed, and mandatory selected tests keep closeout open until target policy accepts the outcome.

Treat release, nightly-full, full-matrix, and validation expected or observed to take at least 120 seconds as long-running. After tracked mutations and focused checks are complete, pin the exact command to a clean immutable commit and dispatch it to the least expensive capable external runtime task.

Put exactly one canonical external-task dispatch envelope in a delegated validation prompt. Select a source-task callback or one parent event wait, require exactly one schema-valid terminal report, and prohibit repeated polling or progress narration. Before delivery, the delegated task must persist the dispatch and completed report in ignored artifacts, validate that exact pair with the canonical validator, and send the validated completion record without post-validation edits.

Require each external dispatch to reference a passing validation of its exact agent execution packet. Synthetic, mock, fixture, and unit evidence may support but never satisfy an acceptance that requires actual execution; validate acceptance-ledger and human-report parity before closeout.

Treat execution timeout, interruption, subject drift, missing terminal evidence, and blocked execution as non-passing. Treat a parent event-wait timeout as pending, and permit one schema-valid terminal read-back only after callback failure and terminal task state.
Do not parallelize aggregate validation until dependency ordering, artifact isolation, bounded concurrency, deterministic evidence, and fail-closed cancellation have independent contract coverage.
Resolve tracked validation.routine policy before interpreter discovery. A strict ignored local opt-in may only strengthen local mode; never write it implicitly or use environment overrides.
Routine policy does not control explicit CLI or lifecycle-owned validation. Required CI fails closed without workflow, command/profile, provisioned prerequisites, and durable evidence.

For each selected routine command, permit one preflight and one execution; retry once only after recorded material state change, recording policy source, fingerprint, prerequisite result, outcome, attempts, retry justification, and bounded CI observations.

Treat spec compliance as unselected and not-applicable by default. Once a target profile, problem-frame workflow, requirement, or owner decision selects it, incomplete configuration or coverage below 100% fails closed.

Commit one validated durable stage or coherent bounded batch rather than one commit per skill invocation. Compress only unshared, unpushed history and preserve approval, evidence, review, checkpoint, and handoff boundaries.

Before a fresh-session continuation, use the registered WORKFLOW-HANDOFF-POLICY checkpoint and durable Git, locator, current-task, target-policy, and test-state evidence; hidden conversation context must not be required.

Deterministic activation acceptance begins at a preclassified envelope. Natural-language interpretation and ambiguous intent classification remain model-in-loop EVAL responsibilities; do not claim that the deterministic oracle understands arbitrary prose.
Ask the user only for direction decisions that cannot be safely inferred from repository evidence or existing policies.
